title: Minimize operator upgrade rollback blast radius with canned transactional apply
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Several customers running Redwood Private in VPC/on-prem clusters experienced partial Helm/operator upgrades that left tenant control-plane CRs in mixed states (some CRs updated, others rolled back or left as 'stuck'), causing config drift and tenant-side failures. Root causes vary (helm hooks timing, operator reconcile races, kubelet taints during node upgrade) but the production symptom is the same: upgrade rollbacks or partial applies that are hard to remediate without broad tenant restarts.

Goal: Reduce blast radius of operator/Helm upgrade failures by introducing a 'canned transactional apply' path and preflight sandbox validation so we can detect and abort dangerous upgrades before they affect many tenants, provide safer automatic rollback with targeted remediation, and ship a hotfix runbook and operator guard that can be backported to affected clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Operator exposes a transactional-apply mode that stages manifest diffs and applies them with tenant-scoped checkpointing
Deploy pipeline includes a sandbox dry-run step that runs real manifests against a mirrored tenant namespace and reports reconciliation-errors > threshold
Automated rollback can quiesce upgrades for affected tenant namespaces without restarting unrelated tenants
E2E test harness reproduces previously observed partial-upgrade scenario and shows deterministic remediation
Runbook and customer communication templates exist and have been reviewed by SRE/Support
steps: Design transactional apply prototype (operator-side checkpoints + manifest fingerprints)
Implement preflight sandboxing: create ephemeral tenant namespaces, run helm template -> server-side-apply simulation, collect reconcile errors
Add operator leader-election throttle for rolling upgrades (adaptive backoff)
Implement tenant-scoped 'upgrade-quarantine' annotation to pause operator reconciliation for non-upgraded tenants
Create automated snapshot (CR + secret manifest) before upgrades and a surgical restore helper for affected CRs
Add telemetry: preflight pass/fail, per-tenant reconcile durations, manifest-fingerprint drift metric
Ship hotfix release and run staged rollouts (canary 5 tenants -> 20 -> 100)
Publish runbook, support playbook, and customer-facing incident template
progress_updates: 2025-02-19: Triage call with Support, SRE, and PM. Identified three production incidents with overlapping symptoms (partial helm apply + CR skew). Decided safety-net approach preferred to large rewrites.
2025-02-21: Spike complete. Prototype operator-side checkpointing implemented. Proof: produce a manifest fingerprint and store in tenant CR annotation; can detect pre/post fingerprint mismatch.

2025-02-24: Design review with runtime team. Trade-offs discussed: full transactional K8s apply vs. staged reconcile. Chose staged (canned) approach because full server-side transactions were not available across k8s primitives we use.

2025-02-28: Implemented sandbox dry-run harness. Ran against customer-repr cluster; discovered timing-sensitive webhook ordering that caused a reconcile error in 2/10 replicas. Marked as blocker for rollout until adaptive backoff implemented.
2025-03-03: Code landed for adaptive backoff leader election (PR 1723). Unit tests added for leader failover and backoff windows. Creating canary plan for next week.
2025-03-05: Support playbook draft ready. Customer comms template and rollback commands reviewed by legal and SRE. Next: staged canary and runbook automation for snapshot/restore helper.
test_plan: E2E harness that replays previously recorded upgrade interleavings. Test matrix: cluster sizes {small,medium,large}, tenant-count {1,10,100}, simulate kubelet taint/unavailable API server for 30s window. Pass criteria: no tenant CR left in 'pending' after automated surgical restore; total affected tenants <= 1% in canary rollout.
rollback_plan: If canary fails abort rollout and trigger 'operator emergency pause' annotation via CI job to prevent further helm releases. Run snapshot restore helper to reconcile CRs that show manifest-fingerprint mismatch. Escalate to SRE and initiate customer communications using template. Timeline targets: detection < 10m, automated pause < 15m, targeted restore < 60m for canary tenants.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Sandbox dry-run may produce false negatives vs real cluster behavior (webhooks, admission controllers). Mitigation: include representative webhooks in sandbox and run canary on real customer-like clusters.

Risk: Extra operator logic increases complexity and potential for new races. Mitigation: keep transactional path opt-in and behind feature-flag; add extensive integration tests and fault-injection experiments.

Risk: Snapshot/restore could overwrite customer changes. Mitigation: snapshots are CR-only and applied with three-way-merge semantics and require manual approval for tenant-scoped restore beyond canary phase.
communications: Support/SRE will use templated update at T+30m, T+2h, T+24h. Legal and Customer Success reviewed language. We will offer affected customers a postmortem and a secondary follow-up runbook for cluster-hardening recommendations.
notes: This ticket deliberately avoids a full migration to a transactional K8s API (not feasible across versions) and instead provides an operator-driven safety-net that reduces human remediation and blast radius. Plan to backport critical patches to 2.5.x for high-impact customers.
